feeds.title: CraftGossip
feeds.description: Polymer Clay blog is about fimo and clay tips and tutorials. CraftGossip covers news written by craft people telling you about all the good stuff. We scour the net looking for the best craft ideas and projects and review them for you. We have divided this blog into many sub-blogs, covering topics ranging from knitting, crochet, bath & body, jewelry making, scrapbooking, sewing crafts etc.

feeds.title: The Blue Bottle Tree
feeds.description: The Blue Bottle Tree website has hundreds of articles about all aspects of working with polymer clay, including how to bake it, whether or not you need to seal it, and what tools need to be used with it. You'll find articles valuable for clayers at all levels from absolute beginner to seasoned professional.

feeds.title: Clay-It-Now.com
feeds.description: Clay-It-Now.com is your clay art and craft ideas center for beginners and all levels with clay model tutorials.It lets you know when new clay design, ideas, creations, updates and free clay model tutorials.

feeds.title: Stephanie Kilgast Blog
feeds.description: Inspired by natural forms, Stéphanie Kilgast grows colorful organic sculptures on abstract backgrounds, celebrating the beauty of nature and opposing it with abstraction, often a metaphor for the brutal impact of human activities on Earth's biodiversity. She is a mixed media artist with a penchant for polymer clay.

feeds.title: Keepsake Crafts
feeds.description: KeepsakeCrafts has Creative Tutorials That Inspire. If you are a creative person you'll love my weekly jewelry & polymer clay projects designed to inspire you to create and try new techniques.

feeds.title: 2 Good Claymates
feeds.description: I am Carolyn Good and my hubby is Dave Good and we are also best friends -- or more like 'soul' mates. My passion is creating with polymer clay and Dave helps with some of the finishing details. We love to create unique one of a kind wearable art pieces, beads, buttons and more.

feeds.title: Tooaquarius - Polymer Clay Beads Blog
feeds.description: Elaine spend a lot of my days playing with clay. My clay of choice is polymer clay, an oven bake clay, although I love ceramic and air drying clays as well. Polymer clay comes in all sorts of colours, mixes like paints, stays usable for years, can be used for everything from jewellery to whimsical critters to prototyping manufacturing parts.

feeds.title: Polymer Clay Daily
feeds.description: My name is Cynthia Tinapple and I have been blogging daily here at PolymerClayDaily.com since 2005. I've been into polymer art for over 20 years. Now retired, I have even more time to grow and develop this global community. I'm a connoisseur and collector of polymer art.

feeds.title: The Polymer Arts
feeds.description: The Polymer Arts is an informational magazine, not a how-to/tutorial magazine. It is polymer clay artist's magazine with articles on polymer clay design, techniques, tutorials, selling, events, and the life & craft of polymer clay artists with galleries, interviews, resources & more.

feeds.title: Polymer Clay Tutor Blog
feeds.description: Cindy Lietz is passionate about polymer clay beads & handmade jewelry. She is absolutely crazy about polymer clay. For over fifteen years now, she have been working with and have taught many different mediums including acrylic painting, children's art murals, painted glass, glass tile mosaics, punched tin, making handmade paper, scrapbooking, beaded jewelry.

feeds.title: Polymer Clay Workshop
feeds.description: My name is Meg. I live in absolute wonder of being alive! I have an inexplicable passion for colors and patterns. I love inventing new polymer clay cane techniques and sharing them with people all over the world.

feeds.title: Debbie Crothers Blog
feeds.description: The blog of polymer clay Artist & Instructor Debbie Crothers. See what Deb gets up to in her Geraldton Studio, creating amazing polymer clay jewellery

feeds.title: Paisley Lizard Blog
feeds.description: Paisley Lizard is a blog about adventures in jewelry designs, techniques, and materials, focused on beads, wire, and polymer clay. Tammy also create keepsake boxes, ornaments, and other home decor items using polymer clay and mixed media techniques.

feeds.title: Fulgorine
feeds.description: I am originally from South Africa, but I have been living in the UK for nearly half my life. I have always loved making things, and have tried several mediums over the years; traditional painting and drawing, stained glass, digital work and most recently polymer clay.

feeds.title: Polymer Clay TV & Polymer Clay Productions
feeds.description: Polymer Clay TV came out of a partnership of two crafty women, Ilysa Ginsburg & Kira Slye. Ilysa & Kira have worked together since 2006 when they met online when they formed the Polymer Clay Artists Guild of Etsy (PCAGOE). Polymer Clay TV was born from this and is still going strong after 7 years.

feeds.title: Tina Holden's Beadcomber
feeds.description: Polymer clay and Handmade Jewelry creations, Tutorials and eye candy.

feeds.title: Aleah Klay Studio
feeds.description: I am a self taught artist. I've been messing around with all kinds of different mediums for as long as I can remember. I love creating mixed medium 3 dimensional pieces. Some of the materials I regularly use are polymer clays, fabric, acrylics, chalk pastels, fabric dye and paints, copic markers, Wire, leather, faux fur, mohair, viscose.

feeds.title: Hillovely
feeds.description: My name is Hilla, I am married with two daughters. For more than 10 years I have been a polymer artist. In fact, I'am an art teacher (handiwork) but over the years my income came from other sources .lWelcome to my polymer clay world

feeds.title: British Polymer Clay Guild Blog
feeds.description: British Polymer Clay Guild is a non profit making organisation based in the UK, run by volunteers for members who are interested in learning and sharing tips & techniques about polymer clay. Formed in 1997, the Guild is open to all who are interested in polymer clay, from beginners to professionals. This include miniaturists, jewellery makers, sculptors and anyone else who works with polymer clay.

feeds.title: Joan Tayler Design
feeds.description: Joan Tayler specializes in functional polymer clay art. Joan has worked in many art mediums and as a graphic designer. She fell in love with polymer clay because of its versatility and because it allows her to make original art that is in everyone's reach

feeds.title: JBDblog
feeds.description: Ideas, experiments and creations. Art and design from JonBurgessDesign

feeds.title: Meowness.net Blog
feeds.description: The art and museings of ladymeow.

feeds.title: Shades of Clay
feeds.description: Shades of Clay, a Canadian supplier of unique and inspiring art supplies. We specialize in Polymer Clay, Alcohol Ink, Mixed Media and Jewelry supplies. We were a founding member of the Southern Ontario Polymer Clay Guild and are a member of the Craft and Hobby Association.

feeds.title: Mosebacke Horse Sculptures
feeds.description: EvaMarie Törnström lives in Mosebacke. She comes from a family of artists and has always been practising art, has always been encouraged and close to constructive criticism. Her ancestor Johan Törnström was one of Sweden's most well-known figurehead sculptors. Almost all her art is about horses. Through her art I want to show how beautiful and inspiring horses are.

feeds.title: Kater's Acres Blog
feeds.description: KatersAcres.com is a polymer clay company run by Katie Oskin. We specialize in whimsical character and personality driven sculpting. We believe in taking beginner polymer clay hobbyists and transforming them into ARTISTS through our tutorials (both free and paid), blog, and website.

feeds.title: After The Monsoon Blog
feeds.description: Wendy Moore is an artist who is passionate about connecting people with their innate creativity. For over twenty years her primary medium has been polymer clay. She continues to learn more about its potential and am endlessly delighted by its possibilities in terms of colour, form, texture and function.

feeds.title: Learn Polymer Clay
feeds.description: I'm Mihaela Georgescu. I am a Polymer Clay Teacher and a Jewelry Making Artist. I love to provide fresh inspiration, tips and tricks for your work with polymer clay. For me, polymer clay is like a magical clay. You can sculpt it, draw on it, stamp it, paint on it, make embossed impressions using textures, add inclusions, transfer images on it, etc.
